claims.text: The starting material is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder intended for additive manufacturing.
The proposed intervention is substrate preheating during selective laser melting or a similar additive-manufacturing process.
A substrate-preheating range of 400–600 °C is proposed.
Selective laser melting of high-entropy alloys can be performed in an inert argon atmosphere.
Substrate preheating reduces the temperature differential between the molten pool and the solid substrate.
Reducing the molten-pool-to-substrate temperature differential reduces thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients produce a more uniform solidification front in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Substrate preheating moderates the cooling rate during solidification.
The moderated cooling rate diminishes residual thermal stresses.
The moderated cooling rate retards compositional segregation during solidification.
Substrate preheating produces fewer internal defects and a more homogeneous microstructure.
Relative to additive manufacturing without substrate preheating, preheated AlCrFeNiSi will have a more homogeneous phase distribution and lower residual stress and defect density.
Relative to additive manufacturing without substrate preheating, preheated AlCrFeNiSi will have improved tensile and compressive strength.
Relative to additive manufacturing without substrate preheating, preheated AlCrFeNiSi will have improved ductility.
Conventionally additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi without substrate preheating typically exhibits localized segregation, higher residual stress, and defect susceptibility.
The hypothesis is limited to controlled melt-and-rapid-solidification additive-manufacturing environments and may not transfer directly to casting.
Excessive substrate preheating may adversely affect melt-pool dynamics.

The optimal preheating temperature and the quantitative effects of preheating on AlCrFeNiSi residual stress, segregation, and mechanical properties are not established and may interact with laser power and scan speed.
